children: Euronext wheat jumped about 3% on Tuesday to set contract highs, with three-year peaks for U.S. prices and renewed fears of lasting disruption to Black Sea exports stoking investment fund buying, traders said.
A rally in crude oil as fighting resumed between the U.S. and Iran further supported wheat and other agricultural markets.
, the most-active contract on the Paris-based Euronext, was up 2.9% at €252.25 ($292.31) a metric ton at 1649 GMT during the evening session.
It earlier reached €254, surpassing a previous life-of-contract peak from Friday and setting a new two-year high for a second-month price
"Matif (Euronext) was lagging U.S. futures so it's logical to catch up," a futures trader said. "If anything, all extra demand is coming to Europe, not the U.S."
Attacks in recent weeks brought grain loadings at Russian and Ukrainian Black Sea ports to a virtual halt, increasing pressure on importers to seek alternatives.
Hopes of de-escalation in the Black Sea, nurtured on Monday by a Turkish plan for the safe passage of grain in the Black Sea, faded on Tuesday.
Russia attacked port infrastructure and a border crossing with Romania in Ukraine's southern Black Sea region of Odesa overnight, Ukrainian officials said.
A drone attack meanwhile caused a fire at Russia's Baltic Sea port of Ust-Luga, a regional official said, underscoring the threat to Russian efforts to divert exports towards the Baltic.
“Buyers cannot wait on the sidelines forever and are gradually accepting higher prices," a German trader said.
"It does not appear that shipments from Russia and Ukraine will restart quickly while talk is grain port infrastructure could have suffered significant damage which could take time to repair.”
Unconfirmed market talk on Tuesday was of damage to grain export facilities owned by multinational trading houses in Ukraine.
Traders said private importers in Egypt, Morocco and elsewhere in Africa have been more active in the past week, buying wheat in Romania, Bulgaria and the west EU, traders said.

European Union soft wheat exports in the 2026/27 season that began in July had reached 4.16 million metric tons by August 30, down 4% year-on-year, data showed, though figures for several EU countries remained incomplete.
Most active contracts - Wheat, corn and soy U.S. cents/bushel, Paris futures in euros per metric ton
